normative_terms.SHOULD: Any deviation MUST have a documented rationale

implementation_policy.unknowns: Do not guess credentials, provider permissions, commercial licenses, or security capabilities; use an explicit blocked status or a simulated implementation
implementation_policy.changes: Changes to programming language responsibilities, process boundaries, the permission model, or protocols require a new ADR and project owner approval
implementation_policy.dependencies: Choose compatible stable versions during implementation and commit all lockfiles; do not automatically upgrade major versions or add dependencies for placeholder modules
implementation_policy.completion: Mark work complete only after tests have actually run and passed; do not report simulated market data acceptance as real market data acceptance

product.purpose: A lightweight market workbench for human–AI collaboration

platform.later_policy: Reserve platform interfaces only; do not implement or claim support

product.architecture: A modular monolithic application core with controlled local workers; not microservices
v1_scope: Simulated market data and local historical samples
A single workspace with one main instrument chart
Switching between candlestick and line charts
Explicitly authorized previews of trusted Python indicators
product.real_data_gate: V1 completes the end-to-end architecture using simulated data; real market data adapters require subsequent verification of sources, permissions, historical coverage, SDKs, and redistribution licenses

core.ownership: All persistence writes go through a single-writer queue in the core

workers.packaging: PyInstaller standalone sidecar; the build environment is not a runtime prerequisite
workers.validation: Generated protocol types and runtime validation

stack.node: Used only for builds and frontend development; production does not include a Node.js service
stack.transport: Rust/Python: UTF-8 NDJSON over stdin/stdout; UI/core: Tauri invoke and events

paths.apps/desktop/src-tauri: Tauri entry point and allowlisted bridge
paths.crates/domain: Domain types without dependencies on the UI, SQLite, or provider SDKs
paths.crates/application: Use cases, permissions, tasks, and workspace operations
paths.crates/platform: Windows credentials, paths, and process resource limits
paths.python/providers: Simulated market data and future provider adapters
paths.python/ai: Mock AI and model provider interfaces
paths.python/indicators: Declarative computation and trusted Python execution entry point
paths.contracts/schemas: JSON Schema, the single source of truth for cross-language message specifications
paths.contracts/generated: Generated TS/Rust/Python types; manual edits are prohibited
paths.tests/fixtures: Deterministic market data and expected outputs
paths.scripts: Build, generation, test, and packaging entry points

dependency_rules: domain does not depend on other internal layers
application depends on domain and abstract ports, not providers
The Tauri composition root assembles implementations
The UI does not read the database or start processes
Python does not access the application database
Chart libraries are confined to ui/chart-adapter
Provider SDKs are confined to providers
Model SDKs are confined to ai/providers

processes.market: One simulated market data worker with reused subscriptions
processes.ai: Start one worker when there is an AI task
processes.indicator: Start a short-lived child process for each code computation; release it on completion

lifecycle: Terminate immediately on incompatible versions or roles
On cancellation, send cancel first, wait for the grace period, then terminate the process tree
Application shutdown must clean up all workers
Use exponential backoff and a bounded retry count for market restarts
ai/indicator failures must not interrupt market data
runtime.flow_control: Use bounded queues; UI updates may be coalesced; dropping raw data must emit a data quality event with a count; silent drops are prohibited
runtime.stderr: Structured diagnostics; do not output credentials, complete prompts, or sensitive content from user code

protocol.encoding: UTF-8 NDJSON, one JSON object per line

response.error: Error|null; error is required when ok=false

validation: Generate executable JSON Schemas for every message and operation payload
Explicitly set additionalProperties=false; extension fields are allowed only in explicit metadata
Correlate by request_id; do not rely on response order
Cancellation and duplicate requests have explicit terminal states
Fail closed on unknown protocol major versions
protocol.ai_channel: AI tool requests enter the core as ai.tool_request events; after execution by the core, tool_result is returned to the AI worker through a separate request; workers must not execute tools themselves

domain.identifiers: Separate internal opaque IDs from provider codes; do not use display symbols as unique identities

Instrument.name: string
Instrument.asset_class: Open string; futures/stocks are not an exhaustive closed set
Instrument.tradability: non_tradable|unknown; tradable is not allowed in v1

Bar.time_ms: UTC epoch milliseconds integer, the start of the bar

bar_invariants: Timestamps within a dataset are increasing and unique
Updates to an unclosed bar use the same time key
Use null for unknown volume; do not represent it as 0
Chart unit conversions occur only in the adapter
Do not infer the trading day directly from the UTC date
domain.series_identity: instrument + provider + timeframe + adjustment + dataset revision
domain.continuous_futures: Analysis series only, identified separately from actual contracts; metadata declares the construction methodology

authorization.confirmations: Bind confirmations to the actor, operation, canonical hash of all parameters, workspace revision, and validity period; consume once; require a new confirmation when parameters change or the revision becomes invalid
authorization.replay: Operations that change persistent state use idempotency_key; duplicate requests return existing results without duplicate writes
authorization.permissions: Worker role plus operation allowlist; AI has no raw Tauri/file/process/SQL permissions
authorization.tauri: An allowlist of capabilities for the main window; do not expose general shell, arbitrary filesystem, or arbitrary SQL interfaces to the UI
v1_forbidden: Arbitrary external URL navigation or remote UI content

indicators.default_mode: A declarative expression AST without dynamic code execution
indicators.ast_policy: Reject undefined operations, loops, function calls, and imports; limit node counts and windows; do not implement using eval/exec
indicators.window_semantics: Use only current and past data, with lag>=0; output null for incomplete windows; rolling_std uses ddof=0; division by zero outputs null and a diagnostic

python_mode.authorization: Require user authorization for every execution, bound to the code hash, parameters, and input data revision; AI cannot approve
python_mode.warning: Separate processes and resource limits do not prevent arbitrary file or network access; do not automatically execute untrusted Python until reliable OS isolation is implemented
python_mode.credentials: Do not pass SDK credentials or inherit unnecessary environment variables
python_mode.cwd: An isolated temporary directory, which must not be described as a file access security boundary

indicators.execution_input: A deterministic bars snapshot, parameters, and a data descriptor; no hidden global data sources

result.series: array: id, pane, type(line|histogram), points(time_ms,value|null), style

indicators.output_policy: Allow only structured data; prohibit HTML/JS/React/DOM output; validate timestamps, sizes, finite numeric values, and style allowlists
indicators.preview: Temporary layers; failures must not overwrite existing versions; acceptance saves an immutable version; support removal and undo

providers_v1: Model adapters enabled after explicit user configuration
ai.default: deterministic_mock; cloud model credentials are not required to run
ai.context_policy: Minimize context as needed; complete raw market data, credentials, and account information are excluded from the default context; the user must enable an external AI provider before data is sent to the cloud
ai.claim_policy: Distinguish facts, calculations, inferences, suggestions, and executed actions; claim successful execution only after a successful core response
ai.tool_policy: Select only from tool schemas provided by the core; bind every mutation to expected_workspace_revision
ai.injection_policy: Market data text, code comments, and model output are untrusted data; they must not change tool permissions or confirmation rules

ui.layout: Top bar: instrument/timeframe/source status; left: AI and tasks; right: main chart; bottom: diagnostics as needed
chart_rules: React components do not hold provider SDKs
AI annotations expose their source and task for inspection
preview and accepted states are distinguishable
Clean up chart resources on unmount
Coalescing updates must not lose the final bar state
ui.security: Render model text as plain text or restricted Markdown with raw HTML disabled; prohibit dynamically generated scripts
ui.licenses: Include third-party licenses and NOTICE in releases; verify chart library attribution requirements and do not remove branding notices by default

persistence.sqlite: WAL; foreign keys enabled; transactional writes; versioned and tested migrations
persistence.credentials: Windows Credential Manager; the DB stores references only; mock implementations do not use credentials
persistence.cache: The cache can be cleared without deleting user indicator versions; do not mix different data sources or price adjustment methodologies
persistence.log: Record operations, actors, summaries, statuses, and correlation IDs; redact sensitive fields; do not implement full event sourcing
persistence.undo: V1 supports undo for layer additions/removals and timeframe changes; undo is itself a new operation; do not claim that all operations are undoable

fixtures.label: All data is synthetic; do not disguise it as real market quotes
fixtures.generator: Use a fixed seed and fixed UTC start time to generate and commit fixtures; tests must not depend on the current time
cases: Samples spanning UTC dates within the same trading day

delivery.webview2: Explicitly use the installer bootstrapper strategy; first installation may require internet access; the README and installation instructions must not promise a fully offline installation
delivery.python: Distribute workers with the installer; do not require Python on the user system
delivery.build: Build and validate natively on Windows; lock dependencies and record build information
delivery.supply_chain: Build installer resources only from identified sources; do not run download scripts suggested by models; include a dependency inventory and licenses

required: A clean Windows x64 system without Python/Node can install and run simulated mode
Open all three synthetic instruments and switch timeframes; the UI explicitly displays simulated
After disconnecting the market worker, its status is visible and recovery uses bounded retries without duplicate subscriptions
Mock AI creates a declarative abnormal-volatility indicator based on user requirements; preview, acceptance, removal, and undo all complete
AI tools and user operations use the same registry; direct requests for unauthorized operations are rejected
Existing confirmations become invalid when parameters, the code hash, or workspace revision change
Indicator timeouts, exceptions, and invalid output neither interrupt market data nor overwrite accepted indicators
Closing and reopening restores the workspace and indicator versions without re-executing previous AI tasks
Logs, the database, and worker environments contain no plaintext credentials
No worker child processes remain alive after application shutdown
Generated types have no uncommitted differences; schemas and validation in all three languages are consistent

performance.profile: Record CPU/RAM/Windows/WebView2 versions; release build; 10000 bars; one chart; mock stream at 10 updates/s
performance.memory_policy: Record a time series of total process memory usage; after warmup, it must not exhibit sustained unbounded growth; do not claim fixed memory values without measurement

acceptance.test_report: Record passed/failed/blocked, commands, environment, and actual results for each item; blocked does not count as passed

implementation_instructions: Implement M0 first and proceed milestone by milestone; do not skip permissions or failure paths
Generate contracts/schemas/*.schema.json from this file, all executable for validation; this file is a specification, not a completed JSON Schema
All dynamic operations must pass through the Rust registry first; do not add generic execute/shell/sql tools
Keep mock implementations until a provider is confirmed; do not temporarily scrape market data from the internet to pretend that integration exists
Keep only interfaces for non-target platforms; do not spend time implementing cross-platform releases
Tests cover protocols, identity, permissions, and computation semantics first, then the UI
Do not implement live trading types, buttons, or tools as hidden placeholders
State explicitly in the final report whether real data and cloud models are configured; do not exaggerate the completed scope
